author: Warren
text:
This Journal is the record of my thought process regarding analysis, approach, execution and management of trades. Successful and failed trades will be logged here for historic purposes and further analysis. Comments are more than welcome. Like with all projects there has to be a purpose and a plan. The purpose is what drives me and the plan is how i intend to get there

The purpose

From a young age i wanted to be free and have freedom of choice, a tall order of understanding for someone of 16yrs old. You learn as you get older as dreams come and go, that they were more of a whim/wish than anything else..........but the fire is still in the belly. Maturity changes things and you can look at things how they are. I do believe there is a place for us all. But i must get to know myself first, by discovering what my purpose is. Trading knowledge is a tool that i will continue to acquire that i can hone my skills to be a more comfortable trader, this will allow me to;

To create more time freedom

To create more choice

To help others and see them grow

To protect what i have

To treat others as i want to be treated

To be fit in mind, body and soul.

Notice i have not spoken about money yet. That’s because for me it is only a tool. It will come and it does already but it is not the primary. It’s just numbers! Targets, well, i will take what the market is prepared to give. I cannot name a % per month or £ per day. Let’s see that the account grows and i can move through the ranks and learn along the way.

The plan

Broker: IBFX

Amount: £5000

Leverage:400-1

Risk: 2% maximum of total account, could include more than one trade, or trades with locked in profit.

Timeframe: w,d,h4,h1. I believe as a trader i need to be flexible and to work across multiple timeframes, it’s a skill that i must master. The clues are hidden in the candles.

RR 2:1 minimum

Stop loss: subjective to timeframe, but must be in line with 2% risk and lot size

Method: mark and review every Sunday supply and demand zones, set alarms. Use boxes drawn to set stop loss and targets. Entry, to use different methods touch, touch..engulf...retest. quasi. Compression.Trendline confluence.

I will share and discuss not only my trading charts and experiences, but others as well and understand we are all working toward a common goal. I will encourage, question and listen. I wish to grow, but be a part of other growth as well.

author: Warren
text:
Do not ever tell me pending trades do not yield pips on daily supply and demand.

Many of us work and do not have the time to monitor possible trades, but do not fool yourself into thinking others that can spend all day by their pc will make this work and because you are part time, it is like an uphill struggle.

Listen and listen good, the more time i spend away from the screen the better, i personally didnt learn trading so i could stare at the screen for hours and hours. I wanted to be free and earn some nice money doing it.

Most of my trades are triggered by pending orders, so i am not even there when my good decision pays off and my trade is triggered. When that trade is triggered its not just the entry that is set. The whole trade is, my stop, my take profit/s. Very mechanical!

All i do is highlight once an evening possible zones, and if they are good i set a pending on it. It triggers or it doesn't. it stops me out or it doesn't, i dont really care!

Why do i not care...........................because the math works!

I do not think for one minute that me staring at the screen and using the power of my mind it will make the market go my way! Is that what you do?

I just walk away and let it play out.

author: Warren
text:
Infest,

I do Daily charts because, the turning points or zones are stronger and quite often you get a reaction even if it ends up countertrend.

Daily charts afford me time, if a trade triggers, i also have set an alarm that texts my phone, so i know "ok, thats another trade i am in" I do not know what time you have and how easy it is for you to monitor your trade once triggered. Targets could take days or weeks to hit. I would say that if you plotted pending trades on 1hr zone, look for tp on 1hr also.

Rules i set pendings by.

They must be REALLY good zones

Consider the trend

Consider the approach

What shape is pair in fundimentally.

I look once in evening and once in morning.takes me about 15 minutes each time. I may need to update zones, set pendings or mark charts with any additional notes. Now, i have had people say "do you have to wait days or weeks for a trade" Well not with 40 pairs. Here is the biggy!

If a trade doesnt trigger for a number of days, there are always exsisting trades to manage. So you could have 4 or 5 nice trades on the go at once.

Find what works for you, stick to it, master it.

author: Warren
text:
Harry,

You and IF are right, it doesnt take many pips to really take the pressure off and be comfortable. I know it sounds great to "smash the markets" up as some people say. Some days i do have time and scalp a little, thats why i like trading, i decide what, when and how much.

I do not think any job on earth is this flexible.

Compound interest is the key, it helped me build a very small live account into quite a substanital amount of money in 4 years. That sounds like a long time.

When i started my live account i was trading 0.05p per pip or 500 units which ever way you want to call it.

I remember thinking "It is going to take me years before my account will grow enough so it can make a difference to my lifestyle. At first it grew so slow, real slow, coupled with the fact that i was still learning.

But as the years pass, things get more interesting. Your larger account means that you can use bigger lot size, the two grow your account at an ever increasing rate.

The Snowball Effect

I do not think it really hit home until i was able to comfortably place trades at 1 standard lot. Thats the point when all the hardwork is worth it.

All the TV i missed, the facebook updates and all the silly games, the midweek drowning sorrows at the bar. Was it worth missing this for a few years?

Do not put off the things you should do now, because life will pass you by.

Knowing what counts, where to put focus, where to be disciplined, also how our brain works and how to react to negative impacts, to see them as a opportunity and such.

Our hobby is definitely more than "just" trading - it is a religion that leads us through life and the way people react to market situations reflects our emotions and inner thoughts that can be learned by studying hard....

5 years of trading is a very long time to me as I just start to hit my first year of trading, where I only traded S&D since about half a year seriously.

But still we are all very young /most of us/ so what are 5 years if we study hard we can pick the cherry each day as the Ace traders do and let us concentrate on more beautiful things in life;-)

author: Pro Trader
text:
Hi Warren, some great thoughts have been expressed here. Keep it up.

I trade in a similar fashion in terms of using limit orders. I used to watch charts looking for small pips before I found SD and understood it. Watching didn't help then and I don't need to know.

I do most of my analysis in the evenings too. I write up my plan for each trade with Entry, SL and Targets and actions to be taken at each target level if necessary. This has helped a lot as I know what to expect in a trade ahead of time and I have a plan for how I will react. When I started out, I never really understood how important this was which let to frustration over closing too early or moving stops out of fear etc. Now I just set the orders in the market and set alerts on my iPhone for when price hits my levels so I know when I am in or out of a trade. If I need to take action I know when and where as it's written in my plan for each trade. I save this in the cloud so I can access it at any time should I need to.

A mechanical approach has served me well and seems to work for you too. My 1st 2:1 + trades were when I started trading SD and my best ones where when I was no where near my PC. I noticed that if I watched too much I might interfere. If I don't watch, the trades just do their thing and I am right or wrong.

I also check for trades in the morning and do the same thing setting limts etc.

Obviously if market conditions change I may modify the trade but ideal with that if and when it happens.

I mainly trade from 30m to H4 from Daily/Weekly zones but I've recently been looking more at doing ltf entries from those higher charts for when I'm around to catch them.

Thanks
